Pioneer expressed need for controls mapping for their audit, proof of audit-log export, and confirmation of data residency. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share reports and Trust Center access, provide controls mapping and sample logs, and schedule an SE technical deep-dive.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Laura Reid (CISO, PioneerHealth), Mark Alvarez (Director of IT), Sophie Kim (Compliance Manager)

Auto-summary: quick posture review of SOC2/ISO; request for artifacts and controls mapping.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through our SOC 2 and ISO posture and make sure you have the artifacts you need for your audit, Laura, is this the right agenda?
[00:12] Laura Reid: Yes thanks Maya, this is perfect. We're preparing our supplier security section for an upcoming audit and we need the mapping between your controls and our requirements, also we need to confirm data residency and how audit logs can be exported.
[00:25] Ethan Park: Great, I'll cover the controls mapping and logs, Maya I'll jump in on the trust center and report access.
[00:30] Mark Alvarez: Quick note on timeline we have a third-party auditor kickoff 2026-04-15 so anything we can get in early would help.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Totally, makes sense. So first, SOC 2 Type II — we have a current Type II report covering the last 12 months, and we can share a redacted copy via the Trust Center. We'll also include the scope statement and list of in-scope services.
[00:55] Sophie Kim: When you say "Trust Center" is that a portal we can access or do you send the PDF?
[01:02] Maya Chen: It's a portal we control — we can create a temporary viewer account for your audit team or we can deliver the PDF through our secure file share. Most customers prefer Trust Center access so they can browse artifacts (policies, reports, penetration test summaries).
[01:15] Laura Reid: Viewer access would be better, yes. We do need the mapping though, one-to-one mapping for our ISMS controls to your controls.
[01:22] Ethan Park: Absolutely — we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 criteria and ISO 27001 controls. I'll attach a mapping that uses PioneerHealth control IDs in the left column and Redwood control references on the right. It's a living doc so we can adjust as needed.
[01:35] Mark Alvarez: For audit logs — what retention do you have and can we pull historical logs for say 90 days? Our auditors want to see specific access events.
[01:45] Ethan Park: Default retention for platform audit logs is 90 days in the hosted plan; for Dedicated or Private deployments customers can configure longer retention and ship logs to their SIEM. For hosted we support log export via the Trust Center or via API, we can provide a sample export and query pattern.
[02:05] Sophie Kim: Any chance to see a sample log extract today?
[02:09] Ethan Park: I can show an example payload but for actual PH data we'd need to go through a data request. We'll provide a sanitized sample extract showing fields: timestamp, user_id, action, resource, request_id, ip, and result code.
[02:25] Maya Chen: On encryption, we have encryption at rest by default and KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private customers. We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or external HSM for private. For hosted customers we offer Redwood-managed KMS, and customers can opt for CMK with Dedicated.
[02:45] Laura Reid: So if we run a pilot on hosted can we still have CMK?
[02:49] Ethan Park: For hosted it's Redwood-managed only; customer-managed keys are available on Dedicated and Private deployments. There's a small onboarding + compliance review for CMK to ensure key lifecycle and rotation align.
[02:58] Mark Alvarez: Ok that's fine, we were mostly checking options. Data residency — can you guarantee region isolation for PII in the EU?
[03:05] Maya Chen: Yes we operate in multi-region. For EU data residency we can pin your account to the eu-west-1 region for hosted, or Dedicated/Private options give complete control. We'll document the exact services in-scope for the pinned region in the Trust Center.
[03:18] Sophie Kim: About authentication — we use Okta and SCIM for provisioning, SAML for SSO. How does Redwood handle RBAC and provisioning?
[03:26] Ethan Park: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, and we have RBAC roles that map to admin, developer, auditor, and read-only support. SCIM can sync groups to those RBAC roles. We also have session/session timeout policies and MFA enforced via SSO provider policies.
[03:40] Laura Reid: For our auditors we need to show separation of duties, so we'd like to see role definitions and evidence of provisioning events. Is that in your audit artifacts?
[03:50] Maya Chen: Yes role definitions and provisioning logs are part of the artifacts we keep. We'll surface a sample of provisioning events from SCIM and the admin activity logs.
[03:58] Mark Alvarez: On logs again — how granular are request logs for inference calls? We need to show request origin and any egress of data.
[04:06] Ethan Park: Request logs include request-id, model, route, originating IP, timestamp, and response status. We do not include full prompt contents in platform-level logs by default; prompt-level telemetry is stored separately and can be turned on with consent or in Dedicated where you can control retention. We'll add notes about redaction and PII handling.
[04:25] Sophie Kim: Do you have a documented controls mapping for prompt data access and masking?
[04:29] Ethan Park: Yes, in the controls mapping doc there's a section on data handling, redaction, and masking controls. We'll flag that for you.
[04:36] Laura Reid: Can you confirm which of your controls are audited as part of SOC 2 vs ISO 27001? Our auditors want to see crosswalk.
[04:45] Maya Chen: We'll include a SOC2 <-> ISO27001 crosswalk in the mapping spreadsheet. That'll show the control IDs and the evidence locations in the Trust Center.
[04:55] Mark Alvarez: Any third-party certifications or penetration tests we should call out?
[04:59] Maya Chen: We have annual pentests and vulnerability scans; summary reports and remediation notes are in the Trust Center. We also have a current security incident response plan and tabletop exercises notes.
[05:10] Sophie Kim: Regarding SLA for Dedicated, we need the objective figures because our procurement needs the numbers.
[05:14] Maya Chen: That's more a procurement topic but we can include the SLA doc in the artifact bundle.
[05:18] Laura Reid: Ok great. Anything else from your side?
[05:20] Ethan Park: A couple of technical clarifications — when you ask for audit log export, do you want a periodic push to your S3 or on-demand exports?
[05:30] Laura Reid: Prefer push to our S3 bucket for the pilot, but we want ability to run ad-hoc queries for auditor requests.
[05:36] Ethan Park: We can support both. For push to S3 we'll need an IAM role from Pioneer and we'll document the schema for delivered files. For ad-hoc queries we'll share API endpoints and sample queries.
[05:48] Maya Chen: Alright I'll summarize next steps now. We'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary via Trust Center and create a temporary viewer account for your audit team. Ethan will attach the controls mapping spreadsheet and sample audit-log extract. We'll schedule an SE technical deep dive to walk through S3 export and KMS config — is the week of 2026-04-06 workable?
[06:08] Laura Reid: Week of 4/6 works, preferably early in the week.
[06:12] Mark Alvarez: We'll aim to have the S3 bucket and IAM ready by then.
[06:15] Sophie Kim: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[06:18] Maya Chen: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up by email with artifacts and meeting invite for the technical deep dive.

[End of transcript]
